references.text: Jesus prepares the woman at the well for worship no longer being bound to a specific place ([ref:Joh 4:21|John 4:21]), which is further explained in verse 23 where true worshippers shall worship in spirit and truth.
The following verse ([ref:Joh 4:24|John 4:24]) gives the reason for worship in spirit and truth: "God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth."
The Word became flesh and was full of grace and truth ([ref:Joh 1:14|John 1:14]). Jesus is the very truth that true worship must be rooted in.
Jesus declares himself to be the way, the truth, and the life ([ref:Joh 14:6|John 14:6]), which supports that worship "in truth" is worship through him.
Jesus promises the Holy Spirit, the Spirit of truth ([ref:Joh 14:16-17|John 14:16–17]), who makes it possible to worship the Father "in spirit and truth".
The Spirit of truth will guide the disciples into all truth ([ref:Joh 16:13|John 16:13]), and this is linked to the spiritual worship that the Father seeks.
Paul describes the true circumcised as "we who serve by God's Spirit and boast in Christ Jesus" ([ref:Fil 3:3|Philippians 3:3]), a parallel to the true worshippers who worship in spirit.
Paul urges believers to present their bodies as a living and holy sacrifice – a spiritual act of worship ([ref:Rom 12:1|Romans 12:1]), which expresses worship in spirit and truth.
The Spirit helps us in our weakness in prayer ([ref:Rom 8:26|Romans 8:26]), which underscores the Spirit's role in true worship.
"The Lord is near to all who call on him, to all who call on him in truth" ([ref:Sal 145:18|Psalms 145:18]). Already in the Old Testament there is a requirement to call upon God in truth.
"You desire truth in the innermost being" ([ref:Sal 51:8|Psalms 51:8]) – God seeks sincerity and truth in the depths of the heart, which points toward worship in spirit and truth.
"The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit" ([ref:Sal 51:19|Psalms 51:19]) – true worship concerns the inner, spiritual relationship with God, not merely external rituals.
Believers are urged to be filled with the Spirit and to sing praises to the Lord from their whole heart ([ref:Ef 5:18-20|Ephesians 5:18–20]), which is an expression of worship in spirit.
"You shall seek me, and you will find me when you seek me with all your heart" ([ref:Jer 29:13|Jeremiah 29:13]). The Father seeks true worshippers – those who seek him wholeheartedly.
The command to love the Lord with all your heart, soul, and strength ([ref:5 Mos 6:5|Deuteronomy 6:5]) points toward the true, wholehearted worship that Jesus speaks of.
